orders.rationale: The two answers have the same content and differ only in how NaHCO3 is formatted, which is a style choice. Both correctly say baking powder is bicarbonate plus acid. Neither clearly says baking soda is pure sodium bicarbonate that needs an acid from the recipe. Both also muddle the metallic-taste point. So it's a tie.

The two answers have the same content and differ only in how NaHCO3 is written: A uses LaTeX, B uses plain text. Both correctly say baking powder is bicarbonate plus an acid. Neither says plainly that baking soda is just sodium bicarbonate and needs an acid from the recipe. The sentence about the metallic taste is muddled. Since neither is clearly better, this is a tie.

The two answers are effectively the same. Both are correct that the Mongol Empire was larger. Both also say the Pacific-to-Caspian span and the "twice Rome" comparison applied "at its height," but the source ties them to Genghis Khan's death in 1227. B has a leftover "COMPUTED:" label and A has a fragment sentence, so B is only marginally less polished. Neither is clearly better.

Both correctly say the Mongol Empire was bigger (about 24M vs 5–6M km²). Both say "twice the size" without explaining why their own figures give about 4x. Both also tie "Pacific to Caspian" to the empire's height, though the source covers Ögedei's era. Otherwise they are the same, but A shows a leftover "COMPUTED:" label, so B reads slightly cleaner.

It also adds ranking claims (26th in the world, 5th in Europe) that are tangential and questionable.
